summary: A single-room expense ledger built with React Native and Expo. All group data lives in one Context backed by a useReducer, pure utility functions do the money maths, and AsyncStorage persists the ledger on the device. Three tabs (Balances, Activity, Roommates) plus an Add-expense modal read and change that shared state.

techStack.name: React Native + Expo
techStack.reason: One JavaScript codebase for Android and iOS, testable instantly in Expo Go.

techStack.name: JavaScript (ES2022)
techStack.reason: Modern syntax like optional chaining and object spread keeps reducer updates short.

techStack.name: Context + useReducer
techStack.reason: Four screens share the same group data, and every change is a named action that is easy to follow.

techStack.name: AsyncStorage
techStack.reason: Saves the whole ledger as JSON on the device, so it survives restarts without a backend.

techStack.name: @expo/vector-icons (Ionicons)
techStack.reason: Recognisable category and tab icons with no image assets.

techStack.name: expo-linear-gradient + expo-haptics
techStack.reason: A polished balance card and tactile feedback when a payment is recorded.

stateManagement.description: GroupProvider owns the whole group in a reducer; screens call named actions like addExpense or settleUp through useGroup(). Balances are derived with useMemo in useBalances(), never stored.

persistence.description: The provider loads the saved group on startup (falling back to sample data) and saves the entire ledger after every change, but only once loading has finished.

buildSteps.title: Tokens and money maths
buildSteps.description: Start with the design tokens and the money helpers. Storing paise as integers from day one avoids a whole class of rounding bugs.

buildSteps.title: Balances and settle-up algorithm
buildSteps.description: Write the balance calculation and greedy settle-up as pure functions, plus sample data to exercise them.

buildSteps.title: Shared state with Context
buildSteps.description: A reducer handles every change as an action; the provider loads and saves the ledger and exposes useGroup and useBalances.

buildSteps.title: Reusable components
buildSteps.description: Avatar and TabBar are small presentational components used across screens.

buildSteps.title: Build the four screens
buildSteps.description: Balances, Activity and Roommates read the shared state; the Add-expense form validates input before dispatching.

buildSteps.title: Wire up navigation
buildSteps.description: App.js wraps everything in the providers and switches tabs and the modal with plain state.

risks.risk: Floating-point rounding makes balances drift by a paisa.
risks.mitigation: Store integer paise and split with splitEvenly so shares always add up to the total.

risks.risk: Deleting a roommate with an open balance makes money disappear.
risks.mitigation: Block removal until their balance is zero and explain why in an alert.

risks.risk: Stored balances get out of sync with the history.
risks.mitigation: Never store balances; derive them from expenses and payments with useMemo.

risks.risk: Only one phone has the data.
risks.mitigation: Make this explicit in the scope note; add a backend with sync after the MVP.

futureIdeas: Sync the room across everyone's phone with a backend such as Supabase or Firebase
